pr_title: sql/pgwire: min/max report correct return type for prepared statements
pr_body:
fixes #54016
fixes #55313 

When using a prepared statement, the optimizer is used in order to
determine the type OIDs of the resulting row. Since the min/max
aggregates had an overload that used a fix return type, min/max over
INT4 columns were reported as INT8. However, when it came to execution
time, they would in fact be INT4. This confuses drivers, and in the case
of pgx and pgjdbc, causes a runtime exception because the wrong number
of bytes was returned (it had to read 4 bytes for something we reported
was an 8 byte column).

Now, the min/max overloads return the same type as the argument type.
This allows us to remove special-case logic in the vectorized engine for
int64s. It also requires an update to how the engine calculates the
return type of window functions.

Also, there is a pgwire test for checking the data type size in the
RowDescription now.

The first commit in this PR cleans up existing pgwire tests so they pass against Postgres.

Release note (bug fix): Using the min/max aggregates in a prepared
statement will now report the correct data type size.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/54080)
Or maybe an alternative is to make an overload for each of `INT2`, `INT4`, `INT8` (and give them all fixed return types) instead of just one overload for `INT`?

Hi,
what a target release for the fix?

@ikgo I have been focusing on other tasks, so this likely will not be fixed until after the 20.2.0 release. To help us with prioritization, could you let us know if you are blocked and don't have a workaround for this bug?

hi,
this bug blocker, in my opinion.
any aggregation function in statement will forward to unpredictable behavior.
this bug block usage of pgx driver. 
many tools, like GORM2, use/move to pgx driver, so we stack with old unsupported version

to workaround issue we should rewrite queries and cast aggregate functions result to particular type. this is a lot of work and make system not maintainable.

Any ideas from your side how to workaround it?

@ikgo Thanks for providing that context. I agree that it's important to fix this.

Until a fix is ready, here are some workarounds you can try:
- set `PreferSimpleProtocol` in `ConnConfig`. this affects all queries. there might be a performance impact. https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jackc/pgx/v4#ConnConfig
- add a cast to the queries that use min or max. you mentioned that would be a lot of overhead, but it is a one-time change. the new queries will keep working even after this bug is addressed.

thanks for the reviews!

bors r=otan,yuzefovich

issue_context.title: MAX() on INT2 column returns inconsistent type
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

We have a table with an INT2 column defined.

```
CREATE TABLE test (somecolumn INT2)
```

When we attempt to compute an aggregation on this column, we inconsistently receive a 2-byte field or an 8-byte field in the result.

```
SELECT MAX(somecolumn) FROM test
```

**To Reproduce**

Create table as above and select as above.
We are running with vectorize=on.

**Expected behavior**

We're running in a Java application with pgJDBC. When we receive only 2 bytes, the postgres driver throwing an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` when it tries to read the field from the `ResultSet`. The response field is being defined as an 8-byte integer.

For PostgreSQL compatibility, `MAX` and `MIN` are supposed to return the same type that was input. So, `MAX(INT2)` should return `INT2`.

**Additional data / screenshots**

**Environment:**
 - CockroachDB version 20.1.6
 - Linux
 - JDBC/pgJDBC

**Additional context**
Application crashes with exception when trying to process ResultSet.
